- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast peaks.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when mean reversion is expected; adjust downward toward historical averages.
- Overshoot after sudden price spikes; apply a lagged smoothing filter to dampen immediate post-spike forecasts.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high volatility; reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
- When true outcomes show strong downward trend after a spike, model fails to correct; apply a downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean often lags true mean by 1–3 days; shift forecast horizon slightly forward to align with actual price momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low prices; if history shows mean reversion, don’t assume low prices are sustainable.
